threads.body: The `apply` job has no way to know whether the `generate` job produced a patch artifact, so it will still run (and attempt to download an artifact) even when no policies changed. Expose `create-patch`'s result as a job output so downstream jobs can skip entirely when nothing was generated.

threads.body: This job should be skipped when `generate` didn't produce a patch (otherwise it will try to download a non-existent artifact and fail the workflow). Gate the `apply` job on the `generate` job output.

threads.body: `actions/download-artifact` is missing the `name:` input. Without it, the action extracts artifacts into per-artifact subdirectories, so `${{ runner.temp }}/patch` (and the `-f patch` check) won't point at the downloaded file. Specify `name: patch` so the artifact is extracted directly into `runner.temp` as `patch`.

threads.body: The `apply` job checks out the Renovate branch with a GitHub App token and then executes `.github/scripts/use-cla-approved-github-bot.sh` from that branch. That contradicts the job’s intent of running no untrusted code and can leak the push credential if a `renovate/**` branch is ever compromised. Inline the two `git config` commands instead of running a repo script.

threads.body: `git diff > patch` can include changes outside `policies/` if anything else modifies tracked files during the `generate` job. Since the `apply` job is intended to only replay policy updates, restrict the patch generation to the `policies/` pathspec.
